ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) is a data pipeline where data is extracted from source systems, transformed before storage, and then loaded into the target system. In this approach, all cleaning, filtering, and compliance checks are done before data is stored. This makes ETL highly suitable for industries with strict legal and regulatory requirements, such as banking and healthcare, because sensitive data can be masked or anonymized early. However, it is less flexible since raw data is not easily available for future reprocessing.

ELT (Extract, Load, Transform) works differently by first extracting and loading raw data into a data warehouse, and then performing transformations inside the storage system. This approach is common in modern cloud-based platforms because it supports scalability and advanced analytics. From a compliance perspective, ELT allows full raw data retention for auditing purposes, but it also introduces risks since sensitive unprocessed data is stored first. Strong security measures like encryption and access control are therefore essential.

EtLT (Extract, transform light, Load, Transform) is a hybrid approach that combines both methods. Data is first extracted and lightly transformed to handle basic compliance tasks such as filtering or masking sensitive information before being loaded into storage. After loading, further advanced transformations are performed for analytics and reporting. This approach is especially useful in regulated industries because it balances data protection with analytical flexibility, although it is more complex to design and manage.

In summary, ETL focuses on strong upfront compliance control, ELT prioritizes flexibility and raw data access, while EtLT offers a balanced solution that supports both regulatory compliance and advanced data processing needs.
